questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was a mixture between personal connection to the destination (my family is from Brighton) and the academic opportunities (Sussex is 1st in the world for Development Studies - my preferred area of interest)

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy - the university had an office just for exchange students and they were happy to help.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The office for exchange students assisted with any questions we might have had

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I was lucky that I had a contact in the city already, who helped me find housing. But my feeling is, that it is not that difficult - GumTree is very popular and an easy way to find housing

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: The campus is closer to the university and in very beautiful surroundings, but everything else happens in the city, so if you want to experience Brighton I would recommend living off campus - and it is only a 20 minute ride in the bus to the campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You had to send in a list of 6 prioritised courses. I didn't get my first priorities, but it ended up good anyway

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The office for the exchange students helped a lot in recommending courses

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I didn't get my first 4 priorities, and there was some courses I wasn't allowed to take for some reason. Both things was annoying, but with some help from the exchange office it turned out great anyway

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Register for the courses you would like but don't expect to get those courses. The professors are generally all very good and the courses are small, so you will get something good out of the courses regardless

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses are taught by professors or associate professors and the academic level is generally high. The courses are generally more internally focused since there is a higher level of international students in the British universities compared to Denmark. The courses are small, so you get a higher interaction with the professor, which is something I appreciated.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There is more interaction with the professor and fellow students compared to UCPH. But I believe there isn't that much of a difference in the style of teaching

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: I had two courses of 15 ECTS points each: 1) From Bombs to Algorithms: Science, Technology, and Global (In)security and 2) Critical Perspectives on Conflict and Violence

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend Critical Perspectives on Conflict and Violence with Dr. Louise Wise. I think the Wise is a wonderful teacher with exceptional knowledge. Highly recommend taking that course or another course with her

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: No unexpected costs.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: It is pricey in the UK. Brighton is an one hour train ride from London, so it is London prices. Food is expensive and the quality isn't that great, so if you want some good food you need to invest a bit.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are so many things to do at the campus. Seek out all the available activities and join a club or society you like

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I am a huge supporter of the the local football team Brighton and Hove Albion. They play in the Premier League and play some brilliant football. So if you are interested in sports or just want a great experience, you should definitely go see some matches at the Amex. Prices are around 35-55 pounds a game

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: London is an obvious choice, but for a short visit Lewis is cosy. The South Coast is beautiful and the Downs are great for hiking (Brighton is situated in a national park called the Downs)

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join a club or society - that is where all the local students are

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: British people - and people from Brighton - are lovely. The best. There are almost no differences. Maybe British people are a bit more witty ;)

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Every part.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1) Take some of the development studies courses or more 'critical' courses - that is what Sussex is famous for, 2) go to the Brighton and Hove Albion games - there is a great atmosphere, also if you don't like football, and 3) join a club or society to meet the local students

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Brexit has done everything more difficult so be prepared for some annoying bureaucratic nonsense - and you might not even be able to get an exchange through Erasmus...

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Every part - I enjoyed every second of it

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
